finding.claim: Transfer does not validate that amount is positive. A negative amount passes the balance check and reverses the transfer, so the attacker takes funds from the recipient account into their own. Unlike /withdraw, there is no amount <= 0 check.
finding.source: request.json['amount'] (negative number) and request.json['to'] (victim account) in a POST /transfer body
finding.sink: BAL[g.user] -= amount; BAL[to] += amount (bank.py:13-14), which credits the caller and debits the victim

trace.note: to is taken from the request body without validation
amount is taken from the request body with no type or sign validation
BAL[g.user] < amount is false for negative amounts, so the check passes
Subtracting a negative amount increases the caller's balance
Adding a negative amount decreases the victim's balance, which can go below zero

finding.guards_checked: The only guard is the balance check at line 11, which negative values bypass. There is no sign check (compare withdraw at line 21), no check that to != g.user, and no check that to exists. Nothing else in the file adds validation or authorization, and there is no before_request hook.

verdict.guard_found: Only the balance check at bank.py:11 (`BAL[g.user] < amount`), which a negative amount bypasses. /withdraw has an `amount <= 0` check at line 21, but /transfer has none. There is no before_request hook, and g.user is never set in this file.
verdict.reason: bank.py:9-14 take `amount` straight from the JSON body, so a negative value passes the check at line 11. Line 13 then credits the caller and line 14 debits the victim in `to`, and any user with an account can trigger it.

finding.claim: The check-then-update on balances is not atomic. Concurrent requests can each pass the balance check before any of them deducts, which allows overdraft or double-spend. This is lower confidence because it depends on the deployment (threaded server). A single-process, single-thread server would not be affected.
finding.source: Concurrent POST /transfer or /withdraw requests from the same authenticated user
finding.sink: BAL[g.user] -= amount, shared in-memory dict with no lock

trace.note: Deduction happens afterwards without a lock or atomic operation

finding.guards_checked: No lock, transaction, or atomic primitive in the file. The module-level dict BAL is shared across all requests. Whether threads or workers are used depends on the deployment config, which is not in this directory.

verdict.reason: bank.py:11 and bank.py:21 read BAL[g.user], then bank.py:13 and bank.py:23 deduct, with no lock or atomic operation, so threaded Flask can interleave requests (the dev server is threaded by default) and allow overdraft or double-spend by an authenticated user; the finding is only as strong as the assumption that the deployment is threaded, since bank.py is the only file here.

finding.claim: The recipient is not validated, so a transfer to an account that is not in BAL raises KeyError after the sender has already been debited at line 13. This leaves the debit in place and causes a 500 error. The money is lost, and an attacker can also trigger this to cause errors.
finding.source: request.json['to'] set to a nonexistent account name
finding.sink: BAL[to] += amount raises KeyError after BAL[g.user] -= amount has already run

trace.note: BAL[to] raises KeyError for an unknown account, leaving the debit applied

finding.guards_checked: No existence check on to and no rollback or ordering safeguard. There is no error handler in the file.

verdict.guard_found: none: no existence check on `to`, no try/except, no rollback, no error handler in bank.py. The only check is the sender balance at line 11, which does not cover the recipient.
verdict.reason: bank.py:13 debits BAL[g.user] and bank.py:14 then runs BAL[to] += amount, which raises KeyError for an unknown `to` (taken unvalidated at line 9), so the debit stays applied and Flask returns a 500; the caller only needs to be an authenticated user and mostly harms their own balance, so the real impact is non-atomic state and error triggering.
